title: Sigil-ese pidgin: architecture and early probe
content:
Sigil-ese pidgin design principles developed 2026-04-19 in main session.

LAYERED LEXICON MODEL (scope chain, innermost-wins):
- Global layer: ~30 structural glyphs (⊢⊨∵∴⟦!⟧⟦?⟧¬≈↔Δ†Σ etc), semver'd, rarely changes
- Project layer: repo-specific nouns in `.bro/lexicon.json`, versioned
- Session layer: LLM-coined shorthand in turn-0 preamble for this specific dispatch
- Emergent layer: mid-turn [+] X := meaning blocks, merged by daemon, subsequent turns inherit

RENDER LAYERS (lossless to lossy):
- Mechanical: deterministic glyph substitution (evidentiary)
- LLM-assisted: rosetta stone + substitution + context → prose (interpretive)
- LLM-interpretive: bare pidgin + rosetta → best-fit prose (emergent-safe)

AUDIT SEMANTICS: transcript pins lexicon versions at write time; replay deterministic; mechanical trace is evidence, LLM render is interpretation.

PROMOTION PIPELINE: emergent → session → project → global (same shape as bbox_remember → bbox_learn → bbox_decide, crystallizing over time).

EARLY PROBE (2 rounds, Claude + Codex, ad-hoc):
- Both complied with sigil-ese protocol
- Converged on sandbox-plus-promotion-gate pattern (σ vs μ are the same concept)
- Cross-provider glyph propagation worked: Codex adopted Claude's ρ in R2
- Honest token accounting: cost MORE than NL in 2-turn experiment (~1291 vs ~860); amortization needs ~5-6 turns to break even at current legend cost
- Actual architectural wins (separated): (1) long-tail transmission amortization, (2) density-per-wire-token is BORROWED from shared legend (not independent), (3) structural parseability is unconditional win

KEY ACKNOWLEDGMENT: "density comes with lexical expansion" — compression is Shannon, requires a shared codebook, codebook must be paid for somewhere. Sigil-ese moves cost from transmission to infrastructure.
